title: State-renamed configuration reconstruction
statement: Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $\sigma$ embed the indices of $m$ tapes into those of $k$ tapes, and let $f:S\to H$ be a map of state sets. Let $c$ be a configuration with state set $S$ and let $d$ be a configuration with state set $H$, both on the same input and over the same symbol set. Suppose applying $f$ to the optional state of $c$ gives the state of $d$, their input-head positions agree, and prefixing $c$'s output by a word $p$ gives $d$'s output. Suppose their tape contents and head positions agree on selected tapes, and the supplied tape contents and head positions agree with $d$ on every unselected tape. Then embedding $c$ with those supplied tapes and head positions and prefixing its output by $p$, followed by renaming its state using $f$, gives $d$.
hypotheses_covered: An embedding of the $m$ tape indices into the $k$ tape indices
Configurations on the same input and symbol set
Mapped optional state of $c$ equals the state of $d$
Selected tapes agree in contents and head positions
Unselected tapes agree with supplied contents and head positions
